title: Evaluation of Polymeric Gene Delivery Nanoparticles by Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis and High-throughput Flow Cytometry
protocol: Do not allow cells to grow to overconfluency.
Use early passage cells when transfecting primary cells.
Twenty-four hours prior to transfection, trypsinize the cells.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cell suspension with media to achieve the desired cell density (cells/volume).
Seed cells into clear tissue culture-treated flat-bottom 96-well plates using a reservoir and multichannel pipettes.
Thaw polymer and DNA stock solutions at room temperature (RT).
Dilute polymer stock solution in clear 96-well plates with 25 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH=5.2) to obtain the desired polymer weight to DNA weight ratios (wt/wt).
Dilute DNA stock solution in clear 96-well plates with 25 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH=5.2) to obtain the desired polymer weight to DNA weight ratios (wt/wt).
Dilute DNA stored at 1 mg/ml in sodium acetate buffer to a concentration of 0.03 to 0.06 mg/ml.
Dilute the 100 mg/ml polymer/DMSO solution in sodium acetate buffer according to the required concentration for the desired polymer to DNA weight-to-weight ratio.
Dilute PBAE polymers first to 10 mg/ml before further dilution.
Add an equal volume of the plasmid DNA solution to the PBAE solution using a twelve-channel pipette.
Mix the mixture vigorously.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 10 min.
Add 20 μl nanoparticles to each well dropwise using a twelve-channel pipette.
Incubate transfected cells at 37°C for two to four hours.
Replace wells with fresh media (100 μl/well).
Analyze transfection efficiency visually with a fluorescence microscope forty-eight hours post-transfection.
Quantify transfection efficiency using a flow cytometer forty-eight hours post-transfection.
Analyze cell toxicity visually with a fluorescence microscope twenty-four hours post-transfection.
Quantify cell toxicity using the CellTiter 96 AQueous One assay twenty-four hours post-transfection.
Use multichannel pipettes to prepare a 96-well plate for flow cytometry.
Wash the plate with PBS.
Trypsinize each well with 30 μl of trypsin/EDTA.
Neutralize with 170 μl FACS buffer (PBS + 2% FBS).
Pipette up and down in each well, including around edges.
Transfer the entire 200-μl volume from each well to corresponding wells in a round-bottom or V-bottom 96-well plate.
Centrifuge the plate at 130 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Remove 170 μl media from each well.
Pipette up and down in each well to resuspend cells while avoiding bubbles.
Add 10 μl of FACS buffer+PI (50:1 dilution; PI stock concentration 1 mg/ml) to each well for viability staining with propidium iodide.
Immediately place the plate on ice and cover from light.
Start the C6 Accuri flow cytometer.
Initiate the HyperCyt 96-well attachment.
Launch the HyperView software.
Choose the appropriate plate type, plate layout, and other settings such as shake/sip/rinse/shake time in the Design and Protocol tabs of HyperView.
Set a pre-plate prime for one minute.
Perform a pre-plate shake for 30 sec at 2,400 rpm.
Configure sip time to 15 sec at 15 rpm.
Program a probe rinse every well for 2 sec.
Schedule an inter-well shake every 12 wells for 12 sec at 2,400 rpm.
Use HyperView Well Identification tab to process the data.
Separate into appropriate well using the software's noise filter and base even filter under advanced settings.
Quantify percentage of positively transfected live cells by gating different populations.
View flow data on a FSC vs. SSC scatter plot to separate cells from debris.
If propidium iodide (PI) was used, gate individual cell population and view on a FSC vs. FL3 plot to separate live cells from dead cells.
Gate live cells for quantification of number of transfected cells.
View live cell population on appropriate channels, such as GFP in FL1.
Use untreated population to gate the untreated cells to identify background signal.
Isolate positively transfected cells using this gate and view the transfected populations using scatter and contour plots.
Mix 1 ml of CellTiter 96 AQueous One assay solution with 10 ml of fresh media.
Remove the media from cells.
Pipette 110 μl of the premixed solution+media per well.
Measure the absorbance at 490 nm every one hour interval from 1 to 4 hours until the absorbance from the untreated condition is in the linear range of the assay.
Include four control wells with only solution+media for a background absorbance reading.
Average the absorbance values from the four replicate wells per condition.
Subtract the average background absorbance from each average.
Normalize the corrected average for each treated condition to the corrected average of the untreated condition to determine the percent cell viability.
Prime the fluidics system of the Nanosight NS500 by running the diluent pump forward at approximately 1/5th the max speed and the sample pump backward at approximately 1/10th the max speed.
Continue until the fluidics system is flushed with diluent.
Dilute the stock plasmid DNA (1 mg/ml) in sodium acetate buffer (25 mM, pH 5).
Dilute the stock PBAE (100 mg/ml) in sodium acetate buffer (25 mM, pH 5).
Dilute plasmid DNA concentration to 0.06 mg/ml.
Dilute polymer solution to a concentration based on the required weight-weight ratio of polymer to DNA.
Add equal volumes of polymer solution to plasmid DNA solution and mix vigorously.
Incubate mixture at room temperature for 10 min.
Dilute nanoparticle solution 100-fold into PBS to achieve appropriate concentration range for NTA.
Load sample into Nanosight by placing loading tube into the sample Eppendorf tube.
Ensure no air bubbles are introduced during loading.
In capture mode, increase camera level until particles can be seen.
Adjust focus so that particles look smooth.
While in standard mode, adjust camera level to observe all particles on screen.
Modify camera shutter and gain if an intermediate camera level is needed for optimal observation.
Visually check to ensure there are between 20 - 100 particles on the screen.
Flush NS500 and adjust dilution into PBS if particle number is not ideal.
Adjust the capture duration according to the standard mode table.
Flush the system before loading a new sample.
Open a video file for processing once videos are captured.
Tune parameters to best process the video.
Increase screen gain to better see particles.
Select auto adjust for parameters under standard or advanced mode.
Manually set parameters if auto settings do not adequately select particles.
Click the process button after all particles are picked on screen.
Change the PBS dilution by increasing it by 2x.
Repeat the above procedure with the new PBS dilution.
Measure multiple dilutions of the same sample to ensure accurate concentration measurement.
Verify plasmid incorporation into nanoparticles using gel electrophoresis.
Evaluate for free DNA presence in the gel electrophoresis results.
Use standard techniques to measure DNA absorbance if not all plasmids are encapsulated.
Quantify total encapsulated plasmids based on the DNA absorbance measurements.
Calculate the average number of plasmids per particle by dividing total encapsulated plasmid concentration by NTA measured particle concentration.
Calculate the volume fraction of each 1-nm bin of particles using the NTA particle size histogram.
Multiply this volume fraction distribution by the total plasmid amount to obtain the number of plasmids in each bin.
Divide these numbers by the number of particles in each bin to determine the number of plasmids-per-particle for each particle size.
